title: Credential split by a separator that nothing removes
description: A credential is split by a line break that no surrounding construct removes: a literal line feed or carriage return plus line feed in plain text, a backslash-newline inside single quotes, a Markdown paragraph line ending.
semantics: The text holds two fragments and a separator that stays in the value, so the joined text is a different value from the original and is not the documented credential grammar. Policy (maintainer-only, ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 3): the fragments are a partial leak and are protected, the secret bytes being the fragments; the reading stays recorded as inserts-separator, never rewritten by stripping whitespace.

applicability.rationale: Carrier-level: independent of the credential family.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 3 (#95)): the fragments of a value a separator interrupts are protected and the outcome is must-flag. Cited texts state that the separator is kept (single quotes preserve the literal value; a Markdown soft line break is treated like a space); no source says fragments must be protected, so this is a project choice. The reading is recorded as inserts-separator and is never rewritten by stripping whitespace. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: Enclosing characters in single-quotes shall preserve the literal value of each character within the single-quotes.
A soft line break is a line ending that is not a hard line break; it is treated like a space.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
